item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 242311
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
south-southwest of Honolulu, Hawaii, on Tropical Storm Iselle,
located several hundred miles west-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula, and on newly formed Tropical
Depression Ten-E, located several hundred miles southwest of
the southern tip of Baja California Peninsula.

Central East Pacific:
A tropical wave located well to the south of southern Mexico is
producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental
conditions are forecast to be favorable for development, and a
tropical depression is expected to form by the end of the week
while the system moves generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15
mph, well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Well Offshore of Southern Mexico:
Another area of low pressure could form well offshore of Central
America late this week. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for some gradual development of this system over the weekend, while
it moves westward to west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph well
offshore of southern Mexico. The system could become a tropical
depression by the end of the weekend into early portion of next
week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...40 percent.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. Some slow development of this system is possible
over the next several days while it drifts north-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ25 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.title: Summary for Tropical Storm Iselle (EP4/EP092026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...ISELLE REMAINS JUST BELOW HURRICANE STRENGTH... As of 8:00 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 the center of Iselle was located near 20.1, -118.6 with movement NW at 15 mph. The minimum central pressure was 988 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 70 mph.

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Public Advisory Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 250236
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Iselle Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026
 
...ISELLE REMAINS JUST BELOW HURRICANE STRENGTH...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 PM PDT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.1N 118.6W
ABOUT 590 MI...950 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Iselle was 
located near latitude 20.1 North, longitude 118.6 West. Iselle is 
moving toward the northwest near 15 mph (24 km/h), and this motion 
is expected to continue through tonight, followed by a turn toward 
the west-northwest on Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 70 mph (110 km/h) with higher 
gusts. A short amount of time remains for additional strengthening, 
and Iselle could briefly become a hurricane. Gradual weakening is 
then forecast starting later on Tuesday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 195 miles (315 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle are affecting the west coast of the
Baja California Peninsula, and will continue for a couple more days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 250237
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Iselle Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026
 
Based on the most recent satellite imagery, it appears that the 
moderate west-northwesterly shear could be starting to impact 
Iselle, as the bulk of the convection is being pushed away from the 
center. The cyclone still has a training curved band that extends 
pretty far south on the east side. The most recent subjective Dvorak 
classification from TAFB is T3.5/55 kt, and the objective satellite 
intensity estimates range from 50 to 67 kt. Based on the given data, 
the initial intensity is being kept at 60 kt for this advisory.
 
The initial motion estimate is unchanged from the previous advisory,
northwestward, or 315/10 kt.  A mid-level ridge north of Iselle is
forecast to strengthen, causing Iselle to turn west-northwestward on
Tuesday, and that motion should then continue through the end of the
week.  The latest NHC track forecast is quite similar to the
previous one, and lies very close to the HFIP Corrected Consensus
(HCCA) and the Google DeepMind Ensemble Mean (GDMI).

The storm is still over warm waters and within a moist environment, 
but with moderate west-northwesterly vertical wind shear, there is 
likely a limit to how much strength Iselle could gain. It is still 
possible that Iselle could get to hurricane intensity, however, the 
time to do so is limited. After the next 12 h, the environment is 
expected to become more hostile as the wind shear, dry air, and 
cooler sea-surface temperatures will have a negative impact on the 
cyclone's intensity. The simulated ECMWF and GFS satellite imagery 
suggest that Iselle could become a a remnant low as early as 
Wednesday night and then could be dissipate around day 4. It is 
possible that this system could dissipate even sooner than what is 
currently forecasted.  
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

DISSIPATING ON TUESDAY...

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...14.5N 120.3W
ABOUT 895 MI...1435 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 30 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 PM PDT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Ten-E 
was located near latitude 14.5 North, longitude 120.3 West. The 
depression is moving toward the north-northeast near 9 mph (15 
km/h). This motion with an increase in forward speed is expected 
tonight and Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Slight strengthening is forecast, and the depression could 
become a tropical storm early Tuesday before it becomes absorbed by 
Iselle later that day.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Tropical Depression Ten-E Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 250231
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Depression Ten-E Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026
800 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026
 
The depression has not changed much over the past several hours, and
it continues to maintain a small area of deep convection near the
center. This system is tiny in comparison to Iselle, which is
located about 400 miles to its north-northeast. The latest satellite
intensity estimates generally support maintaining the initial
wind speed at 30 kt.
 
Slight strengthening is possible overnight, and the depression could
briefly become a tropical storm. However, all of the models agree
that this cyclone will be absorbed by Iselle on Tuesday.  Based
on the new guidance, the NHC forecast has moved up dissipation to
24 hours.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/0300Z 14.5N 120.3W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  25/1200Z 16.7N 119.5W   35 KT  40 MPH
 24H  26/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi
